observations: In this run we observed a single-file program (industry.py) grown entirely by scripted string-replace patches and whole-file reads: every later session began by reading the full file ([2.2], [3.2], [4.2], [5.4], [6.3]). Twice the agent extracted shared helpers before extending (invention_sources at [4.4]; invention_setup at [6.7]), while at ck4 it re-derived the success chance in Fractions rather than calling success_chance (diff ck4 l.212). Verification centred on reproducing spec examples: probability-formula brute force in /tmp ([2.6]), byte-diffs of examples ([2.8], [5.12]-[5.15]), and a regression check against old bytecode ([6.11]). Fitting examples drove two lasting failures: at [2.10], after the sweep showed 'No relics found for Jackdaw' ([2.9]), it fell back to the Tech II layout rather than fixing the relic prefix match, a bug that resurfaced in ck4 build-string parsing; at [5.14]-[5.15] it replaced the spec's floor split formula with a strict-under rule to match the split_days=3 example, which caused three ck5 failures and one at ck6. At ck6 it noticed one row off from the spec example and called the example an error ([6.11] final). No memory notes were written; sessions only checked for a memory directory ([5.2], [6.2]).
